title: T2-W · Can wallets help the event-risk monitor?
decision: Passed: W2 (label jumps likely to stick or revert by who is behind them); W3 (early warning from unusual wallet activity); W5 (highlight the wallet type whose buying leads the price). W6 robustness: not all of them survive the 15-minute gap; only those listed in W6 go into the product.

experiments.title: Wallet data
experiments.question: Is there enough wallet-level data around probability jumps to test W1-W5?
experiments.headline: 2,777,538 trades by 147,076 wallets in 689 event markets; 1880 probability jumps with trades in the same hour. Team pipeline: 2 same-owner groups, 9878 entities pass the hard rules, 3 behaviour clusters.

cluster_explanations.C0: higher active days; higher markets traded; higher two sided token fraction
cluster_explanations.C1: higher median gap hours; lower trades per active day; lower busiest day trade fraction
cluster_explanations.C2: higher busiest day trade fraction; higher trades per active day; higher top market notional fraction

notes: Pass rule: ≥ 100 markets with trades and ≥ 300 jumps with same-hour trades.
Behaviour clusters are fitted on trades before the median market close and then frozen (team pipeline).
Types are not exclusive except retail; trade shares: whale 7.0%, skilled 3.9%, new 15.7%, frequent 47.4%, retail 32.8%, linked 0.0%, filtered_out 39.0%.

experiments.title: Large-wallet confirmation
experiments.question: When a jump is pushed by trades of ≥ $5,000 in its direction, do the related assets move more?
experiments.headline: Related assets react +0.01× (of a normal hour) more when large wallets back the jump (95% CI -0.28 to +0.36; 822 vs 2548 jump-asset pairs, 308 markets). Same-owner groups backing it: +nan× (CI +nan to +nan).
notes: Pass rule (pre-registered): whale-backed minus other jumps > 0, 95% CI above 0, resampling markets.
Same-owner groups come from the team's sniper grouping; reported as secondary.

experiments.title: Will the jump stick?
experiments.question: Do jumps backed by large, skilled, many or new wallets hold up better (or worse) over the next day?
experiments.headline: 1880 jumps; on average they continue -3.5 points over 24 h. Significant (Bonferroni): large wallets behind +3.9 pts (CI +0.2 to +7.6)
notes: Pass rule (pre-registered): any of the four main splits with a 98.75% CI (Bonferroni for 4 tests) excluding 0, in either direction; a reliable 'likely to revert' label is as useful as 'likely to stick'.
Same-owner groups and filtered-out wallets (team pipeline) are reported as secondary splits.

experiments.title: Early warning
experiments.question: Does unusual wallet activity this hour warn of a probability jump next hour, beyond recent price moves?
experiments.headline: Out of time, adding wallet activity moves the AUC from 0.887 to 0.914 (gain +0.027, 95% CI +0.018 to +0.038); the 5% most unusual hours are followed by a jump 12.8× as often as average.
notes: Trained on earlier-closing markets, tested on later-closing ones.
Pass rule (pre-registered): AUC gain over the price-only model > 0 with the 95% CI above 0 (markets resampled).

experiments.title: Large wallets and the direction hint
experiments.question: Does V2's next-hour direction hint work better when large wallets push the jump?
experiments.headline: Direction hint hit rate 52.3% when large wallets agree vs 53.6% otherwise (difference -1.3 points, 95% CI -6.2 to +3.2; 805 vs 2334).
notes: Pass rule (pre-registered): agree minus not-agree hit rate > 0 with the 95% CI above 0 (markets resampled).

experiments.title: Whose buying leads?
experiments.question: Is there a wallet type (or behaviour cluster) whose buying the probability follows more than retail's?
experiments.headline: After retail buying the price follows +0.05 points next hour. Beating that (Bonferroni CI above retail): whale +0.42.

cluster_explanations.C0: higher active days; higher markets traded; higher two sided token fraction
cluster_explanations.C1: higher median gap hours; lower trades per active day; lower busiest day trade fraction
cluster_explanations.C2: higher busiest day trade fraction; higher trades per active day; higher top market notional fraction

notes: Tested on the later half of the data only, since the behaviour clusters are fitted on the earlier half.
Pass rule (pre-registered): a main type (whale, skilled, new, frequent) whose 98.75% CI lies above retail's mean. Behaviour clusters and same-owner groups (team pipeline) are reported as secondary.

experiments.title: Robustness of the wallet passes
experiments.question: Do W2, W3 and W5 survive a timestamp check and a 15-minute gap before each hour?
experiments.headline: Hourly prices match the last trade at the timestamp itself (best offset +0 min), so there is no stale-snapshot leak. With wallet flows ending 15 min before each hour: W2 large-wallet jumps +2.3 pts (CI -1.5 to +6.1); W3 AUC gain +0.018 (CI +0.010 to +0.029); W5 whale +0.39 vs retail +0.03 pts. Still holding: w3_auc_gain, w5_whale_beats_retail.
notes: Added after W2, W3 and W5 passed; a robustness check, not a new pass rule. Verdict: pass only if the timestamps are aligned and all three still hold with the gap.
